page: Amazon Web Services r9g.large is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by AWS Graviton arm64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 virtual CPUs, maintaining a single-thread-per-core configuration without simultaneous multithreading overhead.

The hardware configuration provides 16.0 GB of memory, which establishes a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and zero GPU accelerators, relying on remote network-attached volumes for persistent data needs. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

By delivering dedicated single-threaded compute cores paired with a substantial memory allocation, r9g.large provides a resource profile balanced toward memory density over raw compute parallelism. The instance is suited for memory-bound tasks such as small-scale in-memory caching tiers, lightweight relational databases, and microservices requiring larger working memory capacities.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.large is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Driven by AWS Graviton processors at 3.3 GHz, it features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation designed for memory-centric operational profiles. There are zero GPU accelerators and no bundled local storage disks, requiring external network-attached volumes for data retention. The baseline network interface is rated at 1 Gbps. With its dedicated arm64 execution cores and elevated RAM capacity relative to vCPUs, the r9g.large serves workloads including small in-memory key-value stores, distributed cache nodes, lightweight relational database instances, and applications with memory-heavy runtimes requiring predictable compute performance.
